meta.titre: Email Systems: addresses, message copies, advantages and drawbacks
meta.sous_theme: Electronic mail and related network terms

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Computer Science past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A student in Bafoussam is told by her school that a scholarship form must be sent to an office by email before Friday. She types an address, adds a file, and the message arrives within seconds, even though the office is in another town. Email is one of the most used services on the Internet, so the GCE often asks you to read an address, to name its parts, or to weigh the good and bad sides of email. A few clear definitions are enough to win these marks.

items: The Internet is a worldwide network of connected computers.
A network lets computers share files and messages.
A web browser is a program used to display web pages.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### What email is

**Electronic mail (email)** is a service that sends messages, with or without attached files, from one user to another over a network such as the Internet. Each user has a mailbox on a mail server, and the mailbox is reached with an email address.

### Parts of an email address

An address has the form `username@domain-name`.

| Part | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Username | Identifies the person or mailbox | `amina.tabi` |
| `@` | Separator (read as "at"), belongs to neither part | `@` |
| Domain name | Identifies the mail provider or organisation | `mailbox.example.com` |

### Fields of a message

* **To**: the main recipient. **Cc** (carbon copy): other recipients, whose names everybody can see. **Bcc** (blind carbon copy): hidden recipients, not shown to the others.
* **Subject**: a short title. **Body**: the text. **Attachment**: a file sent with the message.

### Where the copies are

When John sends a message to Mary, the mail server keeps a copy for the sender in the **Sent** folder, and Mary receives a copy in her **Inbox**. So copies exist in the sender's sent items and in the receiver's inbox.

### Sending and receiving

A message is sent to the mail server with the protocol **SMTP**. The receiver gets it from the server with **POP3** or **IMAP**.

### Advantages and disadvantages

| Advantages | Disadvantages |
|---|---|
| Very fast delivery | Needs an Internet connection and power |
| Cheap: no stamp or transport cost | Spam (unwanted mail) and viruses in attachments |
| One message can reach many people | Phishing: false mails that steal passwords |
| Files can be attached | Receiver may not read it quickly |
| A written record is kept | Both sides need an email address |

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for the difference between the two terms.
variantes.contenu_markdown: The **Internet** is the worldwide collection of connected networks, the physical system of cables, routers and computers. The **World Wide Web (WWW)** is only one service that runs on it: a collection of linked web pages read with a browser. Email, file transfer and video calls are other services that also use the Internet.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to compare private networks.
variantes.contenu_markdown: An **intranet** is a private network, using Internet technology, that only the members of one organisation can use, for example the staff of a school. An **extranet** extends that private network to chosen outsiders such as suppliers or partners, who log in with permission.

sections.enonce_markdown: A teacher sends a notice from `joel.ndam@collegemail.cm` to the head of department, with a copy to the secretary, and a hidden copy to the principal. (a) Identify the username and the domain name. (b) Say which field each person goes in. (c) State where copies of the message are kept.

etapes.action: Split the address at the @ symbol.
etapes.justification: The @ separates the two parts and belongs to neither.
The left part identifies the person, the right part identifies the provider.

etapes.action: Choose the field for each recipient.
etapes.justification: The head is the main recipient; a visible copy is Cc; a hidden copy is Bcc.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Head: To. Secretary: Cc. Principal: Bcc.

etapes.justification: The sender keeps a copy and each receiver gets one.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Sent folder of the teacher, and the Inbox of each recipient.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Username: joel.ndam; domain name: collegemail.cm. Head in To, secretary in Cc, principal in Bcc. Copies are in the teacher's Sent folder and in the recipients' inboxes.** The head and the secretary can see each other's names, but nobody can see the principal's.

items.pourquoi_faux: The @ symbol is only a separator, not a part of the domain name.

items.erreur_markdown: "The Internet and the WWW are the same thing."
items.pourquoi_faux: The WWW is one service that runs on the Internet, which also carries email and other services.
items.correction_markdown: The Internet is the global network; the WWW is the set of linked web pages that uses it.

items.erreur_markdown: "People in the Bcc field can be seen by everyone."
items.pourquoi_faux: Bcc stands for blind carbon copy, so those addresses are hidden from the other recipients.
items.correction_markdown: Cc recipients are visible to all; Bcc recipients are hidden.

items.erreur_markdown: Listing only "it is good" and "it is bad" as the advantages and disadvantages of email.
items.pourquoi_faux: A mark needs a precise point, not a general opinion.
items.correction_markdown: Write specific points, for example: "files can be attached" (advantage) and "viruses may come in attachments" (disadvantage).

items.enonce_markdown: The address of a pupil is `ebong.paul@school-mail.cm`. Name the username, the domain name and the symbol that separates them.

A teacher must send the same notice to 30 parents without letting any parent see the other addresses. (a) Which field should hold the parents' addresses? (b) What is the role of the Subject field? (c) Where will the teacher's own copy be found?
items.solution_markdown: (a) The **Bcc** field, because it hides the addresses from the other recipients. (b) The Subject gives a short title that tells the receiver what the message is about before it is opened. (c) In the teacher's **Sent** folder.

items.enonce_markdown: A job seeker in Yaounde can send her CV by email or by post. (a) Give two advantages and two disadvantages of using email. (b) A company lets its staff and its main suppliers log in to a private network. Is this an intranet or an extranet? Explain.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Advantages (award a mark for each of two): fast delivery; very low cost; the CV can be attached; a record of the sending is kept. Disadvantages (two): needs an Internet connection and power; attachments may carry viruses or the message may be lost among spam; the employer may not read it at once. (b) It is an **extranet**: the private network is open to the staff and also to selected outsiders (suppliers). An intranet would be limited to the staff only.

items_markdown: An email address is `username@domain-name`; the @ belongs to neither part.
To holds the main recipient, Cc a visible copy and Bcc a hidden copy.
A sent message is kept in the sender's Sent folder and arrives in the receiver's Inbox.
The Internet is the global network; the WWW is one service (linked web pages) on it.
An intranet serves one organisation only; an extranet adds chosen outsiders.
Give precise advantages (speed, low cost, attachments) and precise disadvantages (spam, viruses, needs connection).
